scope: Source-aware hand-layer union and four-attack audit on the complete 27.5-second replacement
summary: The bounded repair passes all automatic late appearance, coarse-topology, edge-energy, and projected-contact gates, but high-resolution human review still finds intermittent finger morph or motion smear and does not accept exact grasp contact.
evidence: The repair changes 23,243 pixels over 51/660 frames, never copies donor pixels onto the resolved flower layer, and runs at 119.05 FPS in 5.54 seconds.
Late hand-replacement violation falls from 11.67% to 1.11%; palette and high-chroma violation remain 0%; projected contact remains 12/12.
The expanded audit passes 11 automatic late gates and detects color shift, arm erasure, hand detachment, and shifted-hand ghost attacks.
High-resolution sheets final-hands-crop-12.jpg and final-tail-hands-every5.jpg retain intermittent ambiguous finger structure.
lessons: Passing aggregate edge energy and replacement coverage does not prove one coherent articulated hand.
Adversarial review must include human inspection of localized high-resolution crops, not only dense full-frame sheets.
limitations: The donor is another generated hypothesis rather than paired clean robot footage.
Persistent per-stem identity, depth order, force closure, collision safety, and real execution are unverified.
next_actions: Evaluate a contact-conditioned adapter on a temporally held-out late window and reject full model-only expansion if hand structure does not improve.
